reviews.title: Could be great, but isn’t
reviews.text:
I’ll compare Rover and Wag! Later on. But let’s start with Wag!
It’s got really nice graphics that are pretty easy to understand. Sadly it is not super user friendly and has a lot of communication issues that can get you held from taking new clients. There is no direct customer service line (only emergency and 911), no option for modification requests, and no requirements for clients to put down info on their pets. I have encountered multiple dogs whose owners do not leave out or even mention a harness for their extremely strong dog. Often, these owners are not contactable in the moment. Wag connects you with an AI “helpline” that does nothing but provide a submission form. Then you get an email from the company. 
It can be hard to make any money as available bookings can be miles apart. I would say this app is worth it if you know your community of dogs is on here or you are able to drive. 
Comparing Wag to Rover, I would say this is a much more last minute, driver involved app. Most are looking for someone to be there in 25 minutes to walk their dog bc they’re stuck late at work. Or they’re searching for someone to dog-sit over the holidays. 
Rover is for owners who see a schedule that matches theirs and book it. It is more long term, booking ahead of time. 
I would recommend Wag to people who have some extra time to make some extra cash. It could be so much better but it isn’t and it upsets me, as I find Rover’s app to be way more annoying.

reviews.title: Wag Fails to Protect Its Caregivers
reviews.text:
After completing over 1,000 walks and building an overwhelmingly positive reputation on Wag, I was suspended over serious allegations of animal mistreatment that I categorically deny.

For over a week, I was unable to work or earn income to provide for my two-month-old son. My account was eventually reinstated, yet Wag never confirmed to me that evidence substantiating these accusations had been presented.

Despite reinstating my account, Wag refused to remove the damaging public review. When I questioned whether false accusations and reputational harm violated their guidelines, their representative repeatedly stated that customers are entitled to describe their experiences.

Apparently, protecting a customer’s right to leave a review takes priority over providing caregivers with a meaningful process to challenge potentially false accusations.

This is not my first experience with Wag’s support processes costing me time and money. I’ve invested tremendous effort into building my reputation, only to discover how vulnerable my livelihood is when serious accusations arise.

Reinstating my account doesn’t restore my lost income, erase the damage to my reputation, or return the time taken away from my family.

Caregivers deserve accountability, transparency, and fair treatment. Wag needs to do better.

reviews.title: Bad customer support
reviews.text: Since 2018, I have been working as a dog walker via the Wag app. While the app makes it convenient to connect with pet parents and schedule walks, the lack of accessible customer support is extremely frustrating! For example, I arrived at the scheduled booking time for my dog walk. Instructions said to knock and enter. However, I did this, but the door was locked and there was no code to access the lock box. I messaged the pet parent and called her 6 times to alert her of the situation. After waiting 30 minutes and still no response from the pet parent, I did what the Wag chatbot said to do which is cancel the walk.  Since I was the one forced to cancel the walk, Wag didn’t compensate me the standard $5 (used to be $10) cancellation fee for the time spent driving to the home waiting for a response from the parent.  Knowing Wag, they’ll still let the pet parent review me even though it was her fault I didn’t get the opportunity to walk her dog!

reviews.title: No worth it
reviews.text:
I wish I had done more research before signing up for this app.

I paid a one-time fee of $49.99 to become a dog walker. After completing my application and gaining access to the available job postings, I was disappointed to find that there were very few opportunities in my area. Most of the available jobs were approximately 5–6 miles away, and the pay did not seem reasonable considering the distance and expenses involved.

For example, one 30-minute dog-walking job located about 6 miles away pays $9.95. After the app’s 40% fee and approximately $6 in train fare, I would only be left with around $3 for the job.

I take responsibility for not doing enough research before signing up, but I wanted to share my experience so others can make an informed decision before paying the fee. Please check the availability of jobs in your area and carefully consider the fees and transportation costs before signing up.

I hope this review helps someone avoid losing money the way I did.

reviews.title: FYI for Wag caregivers: “Set your own rates” does NOT mean you can actually bid your own rate
reviews.text:
I wanted to share this because I spent weeks going back and forth with Wag support trying to understand their Dynamic Pricing system.

I attempted to bid higher on service requests because some were far enough away that Wag’s suggested payout didn’t make financial sense after accounting for my drive time and mileage.

When I tried to bid above the permitted range, the app warned me and redirected me to change my pricing instead of allowing me to submit the bid.

This confused me because Wag’s own documentation says caregivers have “complete control” and “complete freedom” to set their rates, and their Wag Pro documentation says caregivers can set their own prices even outside the average bid range.

I contacted support because I thought this might be an app issue. After escalating it and providing my device/app information, Wag confirmed that there is no technical issue. Their response was:

“The reason you cannot process it is that the prices you’re trying to set on your profile are higher than the average pricing in your area.”

So, based on the response I received from Wag, the pricing range can function as more than simply a recommendation—the app can prevent you from proceeding when your price exceeds the range.

Wag also advertises an expanded bid range as a Wag Pro benefit, allowing Pro caregivers to bid up to 10% above the listed maximum without a warning.

I’m posting this primarily so other caregivers understand this before deciding what jobs are financially worthwh

I’ve been told I can’t request walks until November- or I have to pay $300 to reinstate my account. Once again- for something I didn’t do. Please be aware. They don’t care about us. We’re just cogs in the machines. I’m so heartbroken because I’ve met so many wonderful people and amazing fur babies on this app. I’m going to miss them all. It’s just such a devastating situation without any light at the end of the tunnel, and I hope to save any caregivers from experiencing the same heartbreak I am.

reviews.title: Embarrassing Support. DO NOT GET THIS APP.
reviews.text:
I have been a Wag! Caregiver for over 4 years now— it has been my main source of income in-between jobs. I am a five-star Caregiver (I have never recieved less than a five star review) and have over 50 badges in the app as a recent college graduate. I was just recently fined $270 for “conspiring to take clients off-app” when I dealt with an older woman that preferred we text privately for the boarding of her puppy. If I do not pay, my account is on hold from new services indefinitely. This is genuinely ridiculous and even following an email to support, they don’t seem to care about the misunderstanding.

I had seen the issues about support and price gouging walkers in the past, but I have never had any problems until now. DO NOT GET THIS APP. Genuinely any other caregiving app is better than this one. The people behind this service only care about money— not pets, and certainly not people.

reviews.title: Run by the greediest people
reviews.text: The people who run wag are completely exploitative of young college aged students who are trying to make money. They take FORTY percent of your earnings which is absolutely insane, and on top of that it’s impossible to get clients because they have sitters having to fight over clients instead of the clients just choosing which sitter they want. I have been on Wag and Rover for 2 months and I have made over 3K from Rover and have had probably around 25 clients. In that same amount of time I have made like $200 from Wag and only have TWO clients. One of my clients found out how much money wag takes from sitters and the crazy amount they charge owners and she suggested we share numbers so she can pay less over Venmo instead and it would also give me MORE money. Literally a few days later I get a notice saying my account is suspended because I brought a customer away from the wag platform. Absolutely insane. I mean it’s not like I was making anything anyway, but genuinely it is sooo exploitative and Rover has never done anything like that to me. I make so much more money on Rover and if people want to pay on Venmo they can.

reviews.title: Horrible for pet sitters
reviews.text: I’ve heard great things about this app in terms of pet owner’s experience, but as a pet sitter using this app, my experience has been awful. First off, there is zero way to communicate with a pet parent beforehand, which makes zero sense. You would have to first book it, THEN talk with them, leading to pressure for a pet sitter to either accept the booking that wasn’t fully understood or take a hit to their ratings. Wag seems to only care about their customers and profit, not about the pet sitters they contract. Also, $40 to sign up as a pet caregiver is ridiculous, especially considering how much they take out of what the caregiver gets. 2 stars since I’ve heard great experiences on the owners side, but CAREGIVERS STAY AWAY!!!

reviews.title: Waste of time and money
reviews.text: This is the worst app I’ve ever tried to use. They make signing up as difficult as possible. It asks for referrals, but in order for people to give you referrals, they have to sign up for the app and pay a fee. The pricing feature is complicated and has a lot of bugs, then it constantly gives you errors if you don’t make your prices what THEY think you should charge. The app constantly shows you jobs that are not for services you offer, or jobs out of your area. Even when the job isn’t out of your area and you try to bid, you get an error message that says “job is out of your area and to adjust your bid”. If you adjust your bid, it still gives you an error message. They clearly want you to sign up for their premium service, which is a waste of money since they prevent you from bidding on jobs regardless of your settings. I couldn’t be more disappointed in this poorly designed app. It’s a waste of time and money. I’ll stick with Rover.
